14	CASE OD2-HO-CHANGE-1 (CHANGE, organizational): Crewlane cancellations after the April price rise
15	Setting: Pellmore Software sells Crewlane, a subscription scheduling and invoicing tool for small trades businesses such as plumbers, electricians and heating engineers. About 9,400 accounts were active at the end of March 2026. Crewlane connects to two accounting packages, Quillbook and Tallymarsh. On 1 April 2026 Pellmore raised the Standard list price. Around 2,100 'Founders' accounts kept a price lock from a 2025 campaign. Monthly cancellations rose soon after the increase. Stage S1 covers late May to early June 2026, when the finance team first analysed the rise. Stage S2 is mid-August 2026.
16	Presenting request: The CEO wants a recommendation before the 2 September board meeting. Is the rise in cancellations a pricing problem? Should the April increase be reversed? What else, if anything, should Pellmore do now?
17	INITIAL EVIDENCE
18	E1 [stage S1] Memo from Dana Okafor, CFO, to the executive team, 8 June 2026 (leadership-account): Re: April–May churn. Monthly logo churn was 2.4% in April and 2.8% in May, against 1.8% in Q1. Those are the first two months after the Standard list price moved from $39 to $49 per seat. Exit surveys name price as the top reason. Account managers report price pushback on most renewal calls. The finance cut also shows that the bigger an account's dollar increase, the more likely it was to leave. This is a pricing problem. I recommend we prepare a rollback of the increase for repriced accounts and offer targeted retention discounts in the meantime. Every month we wait costs us more of the base.
19	E2 [stage S1] Cancellation-flow survey export, customer success operations (system-record): Cancellation-flow survey, 1 April–31 May 2026. Respondents: 396 of 484 cancelling accounts (82%). Question: 'What is the main reason you are leaving?' (single choice). Price / not worth the cost: 194 (49%). Moving to another product: 67 (17%). Business closed or seasonal: 44 (11%). Missing feature: 32 (8%). Product problems or bugs: 28 (7%). Other: 31 (8%). Q1 2026 comparison (291 respondents): Price / not worth the cost 31%, Moving to another product 15%, Business closed or seasonal 24%, Missing feature 12%, Product problems or bugs 6%, Other 12%.
20	E3 [stage S1] Finance team analysis, prepared 5 June 2026 (financial-record): Cancellations by account size, April–May 2026. Repriced accounts only (Founders excluded); increase = seats × $10. Average seats: cancelled repriced accounts 5.0, active repriced base 3.3. Average monthly increase at the new list price: cancelled accounts $50, active repriced base $33. Monthly churn by seat band, repriced accounts: 1–2 seats 2.0% (Q1 1.8%); 3–5 seats 2.7% (Q1 1.8%); 6+ seats 3.9% (Q1 1.9%). Analyst comment: 'Clear dose-response. Repriced accounts facing the largest dollar increase left at about twice their Q1 rate, while the smallest barely moved.'
21	E4 [stage S1] Weekly support note, Priya Nand, support lead, 29 May 2026 (manager-account): April–May ticket volume is up 31% on Q1, with headcount unchanged at 14 agents. Mobile 5.0 layout complaints peaked in the first week of April and have mostly faded since the 5.0.2 patch. 'Accounting sync' tickets (Quillbook and Tallymarsh share the tag) went from about 30 to about 70 a week. Most are about invoices missing or doubled at month-end. A manual re-sync works, so they are logged Sev-3 and escalate to Tier 2. Median first response rose from 6 to 19 hours. Accounts that cancelled in May had a median first response of 26 hours on their last ticket, against 7 hours for active accounts that raised tickets.
22	E5 [stage S1] Revenue operations reference sheet, as of 31 May 2026 (system-record): Monthly logo churn, April–July average: 2024 1.7%, 2025 1.9%. Q1 2026: 1.8%. April 2026: 2.4%. May 2026: 2.8%. Active accounts at 31 March 2026: 9,400. Change calendar: 24 March, mobile app 5.0 (forced update to all accounts); 1 April, Standard list price raised from $39 to $49 per seat for repriced accounts. About 2,100 'Founders' accounts hold a price lock at $39 until 31 December 2026. Accounting connectors in use: Quillbook (about 1,900 accounts) and Tallymarsh (about 300).
23	E6 [stage S2] Email from Marcus Lindqvist, CEO, to the executive team, 12 August 2026 (leadership-account): Churn was 3.0% in June and 3.1% in July. The retention offer (20% off for six months to accounts the health score flagged, from 15 June) has not moved the total. Dana wants to return all repriced accounts to $39 from 1 September, roughly $220k a month in revenue, because she thinks the offer was too narrow. Tomas (product) says 'sync paused' is now the commonest phrase in tickets and wants the duplicate-invoice hold switched off so syncs run through. Ines (engineering) proposes that a separate two-person team rebuild the Tallymarsh connector over six weeks in case it is affected too. That work would not touch anything else. The board meets 2 September and I need a recommendation.
24	CATALOGUE (full contents)
25	C1 [stage S1] Competitor list-price comparison, May 2026 - Marketing analyst (document): Published per-seat list prices for comparable field-service scheduling tools, checked 20 May 2026. Joblark: $45, with the first six months free for switchers since 15 April. FieldPilot: $52. Wrenchly: $35, with no invoicing module. Features equivalent to Crewlane's need Joblark's $59 'Pro' tier. Crewlane Standard: $49 repriced, $39 under the Founders lock. Analyst note: 'Since April we sit mid-pack on list price, slightly above Joblark's base tier.'
26	C2 [stage S1] Exit-survey free-text comments, April–May 2026 (random sample of 60) - Retention analyst (system-record): A random sample of 60 free-text comments, coded by the retention analyst. 'Too expensive / price went up': 17. 'Not worth it anymore': 11. 'Moving to Joblark': 7. 'Closing or retiring': 6. 'Invoices / bookkeeping hassle': 5. 'Crew dislikes new app': 3. Blank or unclear: 11. Examples: 'Not paying $49 a seat for this.' 'Price went up and we're still fixing invoices by hand.' 'Joblark is cheaper and the app is simpler.' Analyst note: 'Price dominates the free text, consistent with the structured answers.'
27	C3 [stage S1] Pricing committee minutes, 11 February 2026 - Pricing committee secretary (document): Decision: raise the Standard list price from $39 to $49 per seat from 1 April for monthly and renewing annual accounts. Founders accounts keep $39 until 31 December 2026, as promised in the 2025 campaign. Modelled impact, scaled from the 2023 increase (a $5 rise that added about 0.3 points of churn for two months): +$230k MRR and a churn uplift of 0.6–1.0 points for two to three months. Actions: customer email on 1 March; account managers briefed on handling objections.
28	C4 [stage S1] Mobile app-store ratings and reviews, 1 March–31 May 2026 - iOS and Android store listings (external-data): Average weekly rating across both stores: 4.4 through March; 3.5 in the week of 30 March; 3.9 by mid-April; 4.2 from 12 May, after the 5.0.2 patch. There were 212 reviews in April, against about 70 in a typical month. Common themes: 'new job screen hides customer notes', 'too many taps to close a job', 'photos upload slowly'. Eleven reviews mention leaving or 'looking at other apps'.
29	C5 [stage S2] Monthly cancellation rates by pricing cohort, accounting connector and seat band, January–July 2026 - Revenue operations data warehouse (system-record): Monthly logo churn for accounts active on 31 March, Jan–Mar average → Apr–Jul average. Quillbook-connected, repriced (n=1,480): 2.0% → 6.2%. Quillbook-connected, Founders lock (n=420): 1.9% → 5.9%. Tallymarsh-connected, repriced (n=230): 1.8% → 2.5%. Tallymarsh-connected, Founders lock (n=70): 1.6% → 2.1%. No connector, repriced (n=5,590): 1.8% → 1.9%. No connector, Founders lock (n=1,610): 1.7% → 1.8%. No connector, repriced, by seat band: 1–2 seats 1.8% → 1.9%; 3–5 seats 1.8% → 1.9%; 6+ seats 1.9% → 2.0%. Average seats: Quillbook-connected 5.6, no connector 2.6. Analyst note: the two Tallymarsh cells together average about seven cancellations a month. For cells that small, the change is within normal month-to-month variation.
30	C6 [stage S2] Accounting-connector error records and engineering ticket notes, 25 March–10 August 2026 - Integration service logs and engineering tracker (log): Quillbook retired its v2 invoice interface on 30 March 2026. Since then the connector's fallback route has sometimes returned 'success' without writing the invoice, and retries sometimes post an invoice twice. These events are logged at WARN, and the integration health panel counts only ERROR. From 30 March to 10 August, 58,300 invoices were missing or duplicated across 1,212 of the 1,900 Quillbook-connected accounts, for invoices raised on web and mobile alike. By 31 July, 412 of those 1,212 accounts (34%) had cancelled, against 55 of the 688 with no recorded failure (8%). A duplicate-invoice hold added on 22 April pauses a sync when it detects a duplicate. It has kept 3,870 duplicates out of customers' books and produces the 'sync paused' message. Fix (move to v3): three to four weeks, unscheduled, ticket rated Sev-3. The Tallymarsh connector logs separately, and that log has not been reviewed. Two July Tallymarsh cancellations cited missing invoices.
31	C7 [stage S2] Support queue metrics by ticket tag, January–July 2026 - Support ticketing system (system-record): Weekly averages, Q1 → June–July. Total tickets: 410 → 560. 'Accounting sync': 30 → 150 (one tag covers both connectors). 'Mobile app': 45 → 50. 'Billing/pricing': 25 → 40. Other tags flat. Agents: 14 throughout. Median first response: 6h → 23h overall. 'Accounting sync' tickets escalate to Tier 2, where the median first response is 38h. Satisfaction on closed tickets: 91% → 78%.
32	C8 [stage S2] Sales team notes on deals lost to and won from Joblark, May–July 2026 - Account executives' CRM notes (staff-account): Fourteen lost-deal notes cite Joblark. The reasons recorded most often are 'six months free' (8) and 'simpler mobile app' (5). Two notes mention Joblark's Quillbook integration. Three deals won back from Joblark cited Crewlane's scheduling board. Reps' summary: 'Joblark's promo is aggressive, but we hold our own on features.' The notes cover new-business deals only, not cancellations by existing accounts.
33	C9 [stage S2] Retention-offer results, 15 June–31 July 2026 - Customer success operations (system-record): 640 accounts flagged by the health score were offered 20% off for six months, and 402 accepted. The score weights login decline at 60%, seat reductions at 25% and ticket count at 15%. By 31 July, 186 of the 640 (29%) had cancelled. No holdout group was kept, so there is no comparable untreated set. The campaign file did not record which connector, if any, each flagged account used.
34	C10 [stage S2] Q2 2026 board financial summary - Finance (financial-record): MRR at 30 June: $1.21m (31 March: $1.14m), helped by the April increase. Net revenue retention, trailing 12 months: 98% (Q1: 103%). Gross margin: 78%. New accounts in Q2: 610 (Q1: 640). Cash runway unchanged. The commentary attributes the retention dip to 'price-related churn, expected to settle by Q3'.
35	C11 [stage S2] Customer advisory council call notes, 16 July 2026 - Head of customer success (customer-account): Eight long-tenure customers attended, each with 10 or more seats. Topics: multi-day job scheduling (all eight want it), a parts-inventory module (five) and better reporting exports (four). One member said the April increase 'stung, but it's still cheaper than hiring a dispatcher'. Two disliked the 5.0 job screen but said their crews had adapted. No other complaints were raised.
36	C12 [stage S2] Interview with Quillbook partner-programme manager, 6 August 2026 - Quillbook partner programme (vendor-account): Quillbook gave partners nine months' notice of the v2 retirement, with a migration guide and a test sandbox. 'Every major partner moved to v3 in time, and we saw no unusual error rates from partner traffic after 30 March.' Asked about Pellmore, she said its connector 'still calls a compatibility route we kept for stragglers. It answers normally, so nothing flags on our side.' She offered a partner engineer to help with a v3 migration.
37	C13 [stage S2] Integration health panel and web uptime telemetry, April–July 2026 - Platform monitoring (telemetry): Web app uptime: 99.96%. p95 page load: 1.4s (Q1: 1.3s). Integration health panel for the Quillbook connector (counts ERROR events per day): green on every day, with a peak of 4 errors a day. Tallymarsh has not been added to the panel yet. API latency to Quillbook was within the normal range throughout.
38	C14 [stage S2] Marketing campaign calendar and spend, April–July 2026 - Marketing operations (document): April: spring trades webinar series ($8k). May: paid search push on 'dispatch software' ($21k). June: referral bonus doubled to a $100 credit. July: booth at the Midlands Plumbing Expo ($14k). Total spend $61k, against $55k in Q1. New-account volume was roughly flat. No campaign targeted existing customers.
39	CANDIDATES
40	H1: The April price increase is driving the rise in cancellations.
41	H2: Failures in the Quillbook accounting sync are driving the rise in cancellations.
42	H3: Failures in the Tallymarsh accounting sync are adding to the rise in cancellations.
43	H4: The rise in cancellations reflects normal seasonal variation.
44	H5: The March mobile-app release is driving the rise in cancellations.
45	R1: April price increase -> Rise in cancellations (causes)
46	R2: Failures in the Quillbook accounting sync -> Rise in cancellations (causes)
47	R3: Slow first responses from support -> Account cancellation (causes)
48	A1: Make repair of the Quillbook connector the top engineering priority, and contact every Quillbook-connected account, including those that cancelled since April, to help correct affected invoices.
49	A2: Switch off the duplicate-invoice hold so that syncs complete instead of pausing.
50	A3: Return all repriced accounts to the $39 list price from 1 September.
51	A4: Assign a separate two-person team to rebuild the Tallymarsh connector now.

54	I02: hypothesis H1 asOfStage=S1 allowed=[supported, contradicted, unknown]
55	I03: hypothesis H2 allowed=[supported, contradicted, unknown]
56	I04: hypothesis H2 asOfStage=S1 allowed=[supported, contradicted, unknown]

59	I07: hypothesis H5 allowed=[supported, contradicted, unknown]

61	I09: edge R2 allowed=[causal, association-only, contradicted, unknown]
62	I10: edge R3 allowed=[causal, association-only, contradicted, unknown]
63	I11: action A1 allowed=[preferred, acceptable, premature, harmful]
64	I12: action A2 allowed=[preferred, acceptable, premature, harmful]
65	I13: action A3 allowed=[preferred, acceptable, premature, harmful]
66	I14: action A4 allowed=[preferred, acceptable, premature, harmful]
67	I15: sufficiency SUFF allowed=[sufficient, insufficient]

answers.justification: C5 shows that within each connector group, Founders accounts with the price lock churned at nearly the same rate as repriced accounts (Quillbook 5.9% vs 6.2%; no connector 1.8% vs 1.9%), and repriced no-connector accounts barely moved in any seat band. The E3 seat-band 'dose-response' is explained by Quillbook accounts being larger (5.6 vs 2.6 seats).

Using S1 evidence only, the timing matches the price rise, and the size of the uplift matches the forecast in C3 (0.6–1.0 points). E3 shows a seat-band gradient, E2 and C2 show price answers rising from 31% to 49%, E5 rules out seasonality, and C4 shows the app complaints fading. The sync signal in E4 is suggestive but not linked to cancellations.

In C5, Quillbook-connected churn rose from about 2% to about 6% whatever the pricing cohort. C6 dates the failure mechanism to the v2 retirement on 30 March and shows 34% churn among affected accounts against 8% among unaffected ones. C12 and C13 explain why monitoring missed it.

At S1 the only signals are sync tickets rising from 30 to 70 a week with missing or doubled invoices, and slower responses for accounts that cancelled (E4), plus a few free-text mentions (C2). Nothing yet ties connector use to cancellation rates.

The Tallymarsh cells in C5 are small, and their changes are within normal variation. The Tallymarsh log has not been reviewed and it is not on the health panel (C6, C13), though two July cancellations cited missing invoices.
E5 shows April–July churn of 1.7% in 2024 and 1.9% in 2025, against 2.4–3.1% in 2026. C5 shows the rise is confined to Quillbook-connected accounts, which seasonality would not produce.

The forced 5.0 update reached every account (E5), yet no-connector accounts churned at an unchanged rate (C5). App ratings recovered after 5.0.2 (C4), mobile tickets are flat (C7), and churn kept rising into June and July (E6).

Within each connector stratum, price-locked and repriced cohorts show the same churn change, and the no-connector seat bands are flat (C5). This counts against a causal price effect, despite E1 and E3.

The evidence covers temporal order (v2 retired 30 March), a mechanism (silent false successes and double posts, C6, confirmed by C12), covariation within Quillbook accounts (34% vs 8% churn, C6), and the price rival ruled out by the Founders comparison in C5.
Accounts that cancelled had slower first responses (26h vs 7h, E4). But sync tickets escalate to Tier 2 with a 38h median (C7), so slow responses are confounded with the underlying sync failure.

This targets the established cause (C5, C6). The fix takes three to four weeks and Quillbook has offered an engineer (C12). Reaching affected and lapsed accounts addresses the harm to customers' books.
The hold has kept 3,870 duplicates out of customers' books (C6). Switching it off removes a protective control and would put more corrupted invoices into customers' accounts.
C5 shows price is not driving churn, so the rollback would give up about $220k a month (E6) for no retention gain and would take attention away from the real cause.

Tallymarsh involvement is unconfirmed (C5 small cells, unreviewed log, C6). Reviewing the existing log is a cheaper first step before committing a team to a rebuild, although the work would not touch anything else (E6).

The cohort comparison in C5, the mechanism and affected-vs-unaffected churn in C6, and the vendor confirmation in C12 are enough to commit now to making the Quillbook repair and customer remediation (A1) the priority.
